text:
alex_chang: Quick RFC follow-up: proposal for an 'insulated routing' layer to reduce noisy-tenant impact on latency and cost. TL;DR: add a lightweight preflight/admission step that enforces per-tenant fanout caps and degrader-trigger thresholds, then short-circuit to a compatible fallback model-tier (e.g., quantized or smaller variant) when budgets would otherwise be violated. Want quick sanity check before I draft a formal RFC.

maria_gonzalez: Sounds promising. Two quick concerns: 1) where do we keep the per-tenant envelopes (control plane vs policy engine cache)? 2) how do we avoid stale envelopes causing over/under-insulation?

daniel_k: +1 on storing in control-plane metadata with TTL and probe-driven refresh. Keep the envelopes small (max_fanout, latency_budget_ms, degradation_budget_pct) and recompute with probes every N minutes. Also suggest a soft-reserve token pool for burst handling.

simon_lee: Operational note: introducing a preflight check in the router path could add ~0.5-2ms. We should measure. Also how does this integrate with our existing policy DSL? We can't require a full rewrite of rules.

alex_chang: Good questions. Implementation sketch: preflight runs locally in the edge router before invoking the policy evaluator: 1) consult local control-plane cache for tenant envelope 2) run cheap estimator for expected fanout (based on request headers, model selection hints, tenant historical fanout distribution) 3) if estimated fanout * expected_cost_per_call > tenant_cost_budget OR p95_est_latency > latency_budget, short-circuit to fallback resolution and mark the request with `insulated:true` metadata; else proceed to normal policy scoring. This keeps policy engine contract unchanged and makes the preflight purely an admission layer.

Example envelope (stored as small JSON/YAML in control-plane):
```yaml
tenant_id: tenant_42
max_fanout: 6
latency_budget_ms: 300
cost_budget_per_min: 0.8
degradation_budget_pct: 7
probe_ttl_s: 300
```

Admission pseudocode: 
```python
env = cache.get(tenant_id) or control_plane.fetch(tenant_id)
fanout = estimator.predict(request_meta)
if fanout > env.max_fanout or estimator.p95_latency(fanout) > env.latency_budget_ms:
    mark_request(fallback_tier=choose_fallback(env.degradation_budget_pct))
    route_short_circuit()
else:
    proceed_policy()
```

ops_bot: deploy-bot: Canary for `insulated-routing-v1` scheduled Tue 10:00 UTC on edge-routers-us. Add feature-flag and rollout plan.

maria_gonzalez: Tests to add: microbench with 10 synthetic tenants (one noisy), apply 90/10 traffic split, inject noisy prompt shapes, verify p95 latency delta and cost/unit drop for the noisy tenant, and measure cross-tenant bleed (should be near-zero).

daniel_k: :thumbsup: I'll add a sim harness and a synthetic probe workload. Also propose new metrics: `insulation.breaches`, `insulation.fallback_rate`, `insulation.estimated_fanout` so console can show per-tenant insulation health.

simon_lee: A fairness caveat: fallback shouldn't always pick the cheapest model for the same tenant if it causes disproportionate accuracy regression. We should incorporate a weighted-utility constraint: maximize (accuracy * weight) subject to latency/cost constraints. Add `max_degradation_pct` per tenant; if fallback would exceed that, either queue or perform partial degrade (reduce fanout) instead.

alex_chang: Agreed — we'll add `max_degradation_pct` and a tiered fallback chooser that prefers less-accuracy-losing variants first. Next steps: Maria will draft the RFC with the envelope schema, preflight contract, necessary metrics, and canary checklist. I'll include the pseudocode and sample sim results once Dan has them.

maria_gonzalez: I'll draft the RFC and post in #architecture for review by EOD Friday. If you have suggestions for the envelope fields or failure modes to include, drop them here.

(end)
